question: How does the covariance spectrum of training data determine when a diffusion model learns each component of its generated distribution, and how does convolution alter that ordering?

key_findings.claim: A full-batch linear denoiser trained by denoising score matching is exactly ridge regression and depends on arbitrary data only through mean and covariance.
key_findings.evidence: At noise scale sigma, the optimum is W*=Sigma(Sigma+sigma^2 I)^-1 with a mean-correcting bias. In the covariance eigenbasis, gradient-flow weight error decays exponentially at rate proportional to sigma^2+lambda_k.

key_findings.claim: For aligned linear and deep-linear models, generated covariance modes emerge in descending target variance with an approximately inverse-variance time law.
key_findings.evidence: Solving the probability-flow ODE during training yields sigmoidal variance trajectories and first-passage time tau*_k proportional to lambda_k^-alpha with alpha near one. The symmetric two-layer solution gives tau*=log(2)/(8 eta lambda_k).

key_findings.claim: Nonlinear MLP diffusion experiments retain an attenuated covariance spectral bias on natural images.
key_findings.evidence: On FFHQ32, increasing and decreasing covariance modes have emergence-time exponents -0.48 (R2 0.97, 57 modes) and -0.35 (R2 0.92, 2,914 modes) after excluding modes initialized near target; analogous ordering appears on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and AFHQ32.

key_findings.claim: Wide convolutional U-Nets do not exhibit the main covariance-mode scaling law.
key_findings.evidence: FFHQ convolutional U-Net modes rise or decay nearly together, producing an effective alpha near zero. Channel-width ablations indicate narrow networks recover stronger ordering, while locality couples many Fourier modes and weight sharing accelerates them.

key_findings.claim: The theory explains a Gaussian approximation of distribution learning, not full semantic feature emergence in modern diffusion models.
key_findings.evidence: Linear denoisers can generate only Gaussian distributions, circular convolutions only stationary Gaussian processes, and exact sampling dynamics require commuting/aligned weights. The 96-page extension documents deviations but leaves practical nonlinear convolutional theory open.

method.core_idea: Solve denoiser gradient flow and the nested probability-flow sampler mode by mode, then test whether predicted emergence-time scaling survives nonlinear MLPs and convolutional U-Nets.
method.mechanism: Independent linear denoisers at each noise scale reduce DSM to ridge regression. Covariance-aligned initialization makes weights commute across noise, allowing a closed-form Gaussian generated covariance throughout training. Deep-linear and circular/full- or local-convolution parameterizations expose depth, Fourier, patch-covariance, and weight-sharing effects. Simulations and EDM-style MLP/CNN U-Nets measure first passage of generated variance along data eigenmodes.
assumptions: Full-batch gradient flow approximates stochastic diffusion training.
Noise scales can be analyzed as independently parameterized denoisers.
Weights align with or commute in the data/Fourier eigenbasis.
Covariance-mode variance is a meaningful proxy for perceptual feature learning.
First passage to a geometric-mean threshold robustly defines emergence.

techniques.role: Reduces arbitrary-data linear DSM to mean/covariance learning.
Derives convergence rates along covariance eigenvectors.
Maps denoiser learning into generated-distribution variance trajectories.
Shows weight sharing and locality couple spectral modes.
Fits emergence time against target eigenvalue in nonlinear networks.

evaluations.setting: Analytic one-layer, symmetric two-layer, full-width convolution, and patch-convolution denoisers.
evaluations.metric: Weight convergence and generated-mode first-passage time.
evaluations.result: High-variance eigen/Fourier modes learn first; idealized emergence time scales approximately inversely with target variance, and convolutional sharing yields an N-fold rate factor.
evaluations.baseline: Direct numerical gradient flow and PF-ODE integration.

evaluations.setting: Nonlinear MLP-UNets on Gaussian, MNIST, CIFAR-10, AFHQ32, and FFHQ32 data.
evaluations.metric: Generated covariance alignment, mode variance, and fitted power-law exponent/R2.
evaluations.result: Gaussian exponents remain near one; FFHQ natural-image exponents attenuate to 0.48 and 0.35 in magnitude but retain high fitted R2 after exclusions.

evaluations.setting: CNN U-Nets on FFHQ32 with depth and channel-width ablations.
evaluations.metric: Mode emergence-time scaling and qualitative sample trajectory.
evaluations.result: Wide practical CNNs have alpha near zero and learn local patches before global contours; narrow networks show more spectral ordering.
evaluations.baseline: MLP-UNet on the same data and linear convolution predictions.

limitations: The closed forms require linearity, full-batch gradient flow, independent noise-scale parameters, and aligned/commuting weights.
Linear models capture only Gaussian mean/covariance and cannot learn multimodality or semantic content.
First-passage fits exclude modes initialized within 0.5-2 times target variance, creating a selection-sensitive scaling estimate.
The central prediction fails in the wide CNN U-Net architecture most representative of image diffusion.
Empirical models use low-resolution datasets and limited architectures rather than large DiTs or latent diffusion training.
Covariance eigenvalue is correlated with but not equivalent to spatial frequency or perceptual importance.
failure_modes: Noncommuting denoisers across noise levels invalidate independent mode integration.
A mode whose initialization is close to target has an unstable or meaningless emergence time.
Local filters can learn multiple global eigenmodes together, erasing eigenvalue ordering.
Mean-covariance convergence can look complete while higher-order distribution structure remains wrong.
Power-law fits can conceal separate increasing/decaying branches caused by initialization.
reusable_insights: Analyze both denoiser weights and the generated distribution because their convergence need not match.
Use the Gaussian linear component as a measurable baseline before attributing feature learning to nonlinear mechanisms.
Treat architecture-induced mode coupling as central, not a perturbation to MLP theory.
Report initialization-relative branches and exclusion rules in emergence-time scaling laws.
Probe high-channel latent representations where convolution width may no longer dwarf input channel count.
open_questions: Can nonlinear local-convolution or DiT training dynamics be solved beyond covariance learning?
Does the inverse-variance law predict semantic feature acquisition in high-channel latent diffusion?
How do minibatch noise, shared time conditioning, and optimizer adaptivity change mode rates?
Can loss weighting flatten slow covariance modes without harming higher-order structure?
What prospective observable distinguishes Gaussian-score learning from memorization and non-Gaussian creativity?

competitive_landscape.title: The Hidden Linear Structure in Score-Based Models and Its Application
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang and Vastola establish that learned scores are often well approximated by Gaussian linear scores. The target turns that static approximation into explicit training-time and generated-covariance dynamics across parameterizations.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Generalizability of Diffusion Models Requires Rethinking the Hidden Gaussian Structure
competitive_landscape.difference: Li et al. connect hidden Gaussian score structure to generalization and memorization. This paper instead derives how that structure is learned mode by mode and tests its rate law, while not resolving the non-Gaussian generalization transition.

competitive_landscape.title: Diffusion Models Generate Images Like Painters: An Analytical Theory of Outline First, Details Later
competitive_landscape.difference: Outline-first work explains spectral ordering within the sampling trajectory of an already trained model. The target studies the orthogonal training trajectory and shows architecture can remove analogous ordering.

competitive_landscape.title: An Analytic Theory of Creativity in Convolutional Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Kamb and Ganguli analyze locality/equivariance and creative generalization in convolutional diffusion. The target adds explicit gradient-flow learning rates and documents why wide local CNNs depart from covariance spectral-bias theory.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim closed-form spectral laws for denoiser and generated-distribution learning, with high-variance modes emerging first and architecture controlling the strength of this bias.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Sections 4-5 solve linear/deep/convolutional cases; Section 6 and extensive appendices test Gaussian, natural-image MLP, and CNN U-Net training.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The nested solution from denoiser gradient flow to generated covariance and the direct MLP-versus-CNN falsification are substantive. Gaussian-score structure, generic spectral bias, and outline-first sampling are prior art. The paper's theory is best viewed as a strong null model whose central law is attenuated or absent in practical wide convolutional networks, not a complete theory of diffusion feature learning.

reviewer_notes: Read the full 96-page pinned source, including all main derivations and appendices on alternative losses, non-aligned/deep/patch dynamics, MLP/CNN experiments, phase diagrams, flow matching, and code excerpts. Four direct primary arXiv competitors were checked on 2026-08-23. The negative CNN result and selection rule for mode fits are treated as central evidence rather than appendix caveats.
